problem: Embodied exploration agents have no reference trajectory, and existing curiosity-driven exploration was untested in photorealistic indoor scenes (preliminary studies suggest it struggles). Navigation and language description are also not studied jointly, so there is no way to interpret what the agent perceives while it explores.
motivation: Agents that explore unknown environments should also explain what they see, which gives interpretability and links the internal state (curiosity) to language. Curiosity rewards can be self-supervised and generalize to unseen scenes, but agents tend to repeat actions and stay near the start, so the reward needs adjusting.
key_idea: Train a curiosity-driven (forward-model surprisal) exploration policy with a penalty for repeated actions, and couple it with a Transformer captioner triggered by a speaker policy (object-, depth- or curiosity-driven).
insight: Adding a penalty for repeated actions to the surprisal reward raises exploration surprisal from 0.439 to 0.697 and lets the agent leave the start area (qualitative trajectories). Using both RGB and depth beats either alone, and RGB-only curiosity is worse than random. Shallower captioners (1-2 layers) do as well or better than the 6-layer Transformer, and the curiosity-driven speaker gives stable coverage with diversity that grows with the threshold, without needing semantic information.
method: Curiosity navigation module: a PPO policy on a fixed random CNN embedding φ (512-d) with forward and inverse dynamics models; the reward is the forward-model prediction error (surprisal); the loss is a mix of policy loss (λ=0.1), forward loss and inverse loss (β=0.2)
Penalty for repeated actions: subtract p̃=0.01 from the reward once the same action has been repeated t̃=5 times, so the agent does not get stuck spinning or walking straight

Speaker policy: decides when to caption. Object-driven fires if at least O objects are visible, depth-driven if mean depth D exceeds a threshold, and curiosity-driven if surprisal summed over the last 20 steps (S) exceeds a threshold

Captioning module: Faster R-CNN (Visual Genome) region features go to a Transformer encoder-decoder with self- and cross-attention (d=512, 8 heads), trained on COCO with cross-entropy then self-critical CIDEr-D RL

Evaluation metrics: a soft coverage score (nouns matched to GT semantic categories via GloVe and the Hungarian algorithm, with area thresholds), a diversity score (soft Jaccard distance between consecutive captions), and loquacity (captions per episode)

setting.backbone: PPO policy with fixed random CNN embedding and forward/inverse dynamics (trained from scratch); Transformer captioner with Faster R-CNN features (trained on COCO)
setting.training_data: Navigation: Habitat PointNav episode start points on Matterport3D (61 train scenes, ~5M episodes, 10k updates, no external reward). Captioner: COCO image-caption pairs.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (84x84 grayscale, stack of 4 frames) for navigation; RGB regions for captioning
setting.privileged: Object-driven speaker policy uses GT instance segmentation from Matterport3D; depth-driven policy uses simulator depth; coverage evaluation uses GT semantic annotations

numbers.eval_set_note: 1008 test episodes on 18 Matterport3D test scenes, 1000 steps each
numbers.extra: self-supervised, no external reward; random exploration baseline 0.333
numbers.evidence: Table I: Surprisal scores for different navigation policies; ExEx 0.697
Table I: ExEx w/o Penalty for repeated actions (RGB + Depth) 0.439

numbers_note: Custom metrics on a new task; no standard navigation benchmark (SR/SPL) is reported. Table II has many more threshold/layer combinations; only representative rows are listed.
results: The full curiosity agent with the repeated-action penalty reaches surprisal 0.697, versus 0.333 for random exploration and 0.439 for the vanilla curiosity agent without the penalty (RGB+Depth). The object-driven speaker gives the best coverage and diversity, while the curiosity-driven speaker gives stable coverage and increasing diversity. 1-2 layer captioners are best.
limitations: Evaluation is only by surprisal and noun-based coverage/diversity; there are no ground-truth captions, human evaluation or standard navigation metrics (coverage of area, SR)
The object-driven speaker relies on GT semantic annotations rather than a real detector, and only simulated Matterport3D is used (no real robot)
The captioner is trained on COCO with no indoor-specific captions, and there is no feedback from captioning to navigation
builds_on: Large-scale study of curiosity-driven learning (Burda et al.)
compares_to: ExEx without repeated-action penalty (RGB only / Depth only / RGB+Depth)
